items.title: BackupDrill: open-source Supabase Postgres backups with automated restore drills
items.summary: BackupDrill backs up Supabase Postgres databases to a bucket you own, then restores each backup into a throwaway PostgreSQL instance to check it restores.Most teams find out whether their pg_dump backups work on the day they need them. BackupDrill makes that check a routine step.What it does:Runs pg_dump (custom format) against a Supabase project and streams the archive to any S3-compatible bucket (AWS S3, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, Wasabi), with a checksummed manifest. Storage files can be copied into the same snapshot.backupdrill drill restores the latest snapshot into a throwaway PostgreSQL container with pg_restore. It checks the archive checksum, that pg_restore completed, that post-data objects such as indexes, constraints and triggers were created, that every table is present and that tables which held data are not empty, and it records how long the restore took.Backups are plain pg_dump archives, so stock pg_restore can restore them without BackupDrill.It refuses to run a pg_dump whose major version is older than the server's. Supabase currently runs PostgreSQL 15 to 17.Scope: Supabase-hosted PostgreSQL only for now; the public schema is dumped by default and other schemas can be added.The CLI is MIT-licensed: https://github.com/backupdrill/cli (npm package: backupdrill). The hosted service at https://backupdrill.com runs the same engine on a schedule, with restore drills and email alerts when a backup or drill fails. It has a free plan.

items.title: pgCluu v5.0 has been released
items.summary: Antananarivo, Madagascar - October 20, 2026pgCluuPostgreSQL Cluster UtilizationpgCluu is a Perl program used to perform a full audit of a PostgreSQLCluster performances. It is divided in two parts, a collector used tograb statistics on the PostgreSQL server using psql and sar, a reportsbuilder that will generate all HTML and charts output.Version 6.0 of pgCluu have been released, this is a major release thatadds several new features and reports. It also fixes issues reportedsince the last release.New features:Add report about replication slots retrieved from pg_replication_slots.Add collect of pg_hba_file_rulesLimit wait event reporting to those that represent more than 0.1 percent    of the total of the wait event observed.Add collect of I/O statistics from pg_stat_io (PG16+)Add reports about:I/O throughput per backend typeshared buffers writers and evictionsbuffer hit ratio and ring buffersI/O latency and sizeWAL I/Otemporary relations I/Oasynchronous I/O (PG18+)Add collect more kernel tuning parameters, remove shmmax and shmallvm.dirty_expire_centisecs and vm.dirty_writeback_centisecs, they were    not matched by the sysctl filter, and all other vm.dirty_* parameters,vm.min_free_kbytes, vm.watermark_scale_factor and kernel.numa_balancing,net.core.somaxconn, net.ipv4.ip_local_port_range, net.core.rmem_max,    net.core.wmem_max, fs.file-max and fs.nr_open,/sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/shmem_enabled: PostgreSQL shared    memory is anonymous shared memory, this is the setting that applies to    the shared buffers, not 'enabled',the frequency governor of all CPUs instead of cpu0 only, the cpuidle    driver, the intel_pstate status and energy performance preference, and    the number of NUMA nodes,read_ahead_kb, nr_requests, max_sectors_kb and wbt_lat_usec of each    block device.Collect and report the limits of the postmaster process. pgcluu_collectd now    saves in a new POSTMASTER section of sysinfo.txt:the pid of the postmaster, found as the parent of the checkpointer    (its /proc entry is readable by any user) or read from postmaster.pid    before PostgreSQL 10,oom_score_adj, -1000 is recommended for the postmaster,the soft and hard limits of open files, processes and locked memory,the cgroup limits: memory.max, memory.high, memory.swap.max, cpu.max,    cpu.weight, io.max, pids.max and the oom/oom_kill counters of    memory.events with cgroup v2 (also in hybrid mode), memory and cpu    quota limits with cgroup v1.pgcluu and pgcluu.cgi show them in the Kernel panel of the systeminformation with sizes and CPU quotas formatted, and a tooltip foroom_score_adj and the process limits.Add kernel pressure stall information and memory events reports.    pgcluu_collectd now appends at each run to kernel_stats.csv the cumulative    counters of:the pressure stall information (PSI) of the host (/proc/pressure, kernel    4.20+) and of the cgroup v2 of the postmaster (cpu, memory and io    pressure),the memory events of the cgroup of the postmaster (high, max, oom and    oom_kill from memory.events),/proc/vmstat counters not reported by sar: direct reclaims (allocstall),    memory compaction, transparent huge pages allocations and fallbacks,    OOM kills, NUMA allocations and page cache refaults.pgcluu and pgcluu.cgi have two new pages in the System menu:Pressure stall information: percentage of time with some or all tasks    stalled on CPU, memory or I/O for the host and the PostgreSQL cgroup,Kernel memory events: allocation stalls and compaction, transparent huge    pages, OOM kills, cgroup memory events, page cache refaults and NUMA    allocations.See ChangeLog fora complete list of changes, bug fixes and acknowledgements.About pgCluu:The goal of this project is to provide a complete PostgreSQL auditingtool that don't need any dependency to be run easily to audit a localor remote server.If you just have a sar output file, pgCluu can be use to draw graphsabout the system utilization only.CreditspgCluu is an original collection of tools built during my work atDalibo and HexaCluster.The tools are published under the PostgreSQL License.pgCluu is created and maintained by Gilles Darold. Any contribution tobuild a better tool is welcome. You can send your ideas, features requestsor patches using the GitHub tools.LinksView a sample report at http://pgcluu.darold.net/example/index.htmlWeb site: http://pgcluu.darold.net/Download: https://github.com/darold/pgcluu/releasesDevelopment: https://github.com/darold/pgcluuDocumentation: https://github.com/darold/pgcluu/blob/master/README
